Hi Kim,

Thanks for the updated MAP — I reviewed the draft and have one gating question for our execs before we finalize: MedStream needs to decide which deployment lane to pursue for the pilot (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). We have two hard constraints:

- Data residency for telemetry and logs (US-only) — this is a must for our contracts team.
- Low 95th percentile inference latency for triage flows (target < 250ms) — important for user experience.

Can you outline a clear evaluation path and close timeline that addresses both? Our procurement team also wants a sense of the earliest go/no-go date so they can start contract prep.

I can loop in Jose (copied) for procurement timing.

Thanks,
Carly

Subject: Re: Redwood MAP draft — deployment path question

Hi Carly — great question, thanks.

Short answer: propose a two-week evaluation runway that proves Hosted for quick time-to-value, with a parallel Dedicated performance trial if latency targets aren't met, and a gated Private evaluation only if your legal/audit team requires on-prem or VPC isolation.

Attached: MedStream_MAP_v2.pdf (MAP with updated milestones) and security-evidence-list.xlsx (SOC2 + data residency artifacts we can provide).

High-level plan (summary):
- Week 0–1 (pilot): Lightweight integration on Redwood Hosted in the us-west-2 region. Deliverables: sample traffic run, latency report, initial QA.
- Week 1–2 (performance validation): If 95p latency >250ms on Hosted, spin up a short Dedicated pool (same region) for a 3-day A/B to measure delta.
- Gate: decision meeting on Day 14 (go/no-go). If legal demands stronger controls, begin Private (VPC) scoping in parallel but treat Private as procurement-heavy (longer lead).

Data residency note: Hosted in us-west-2 meets US-only telemetry; we will exclude EU/other regions and provide audit logs per your retention policy. If you need a physically isolated on‑prem option we’ll surface that cost/lead time in the Private track.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm pilot dates (can we start staging traffic 7/6?)
2) Jose: procurement window — earliest you can review a draft quote?
3) Karthik and Priyom will validate the perf test harness and required metrics.

If that works I’ll publish an updated MAP with owners and a HubSpot milestone link.

Thanks — Kim

--

Subject: Re: Redwood MAP draft — deployment path question

Cc’ing my notes from the infra side — quick technical guidance to make the evaluation deterministic.

Test harness & metrics:
- Use the same representative request distribution as production; include 60% short prompts (<=128 tokens) and 40% long sessions (>=512 tokens).
- Collect: 50th/95th/99th latency (inference-only), token/sec throughput, and cost-per-1k-tokens.
- Include KV-cache warm vs cold runs — cache hit rate will materially change latency.

Recommendations:
- Hosted (us-west-2) first: fastest to stand up; expect slightly higher variance at 95p under bursty traffic.
- Dedicated pool for the A/B: we typically see 15–40% 95p improvement depending on batchability and model size. Good for predictable SLAs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): only if legal/procurement requires it. It will add ~4–8 weeks to schedule for VPC peering and compliance checks.

Perf knobs during A/B: quantization tier, batching window, prefetch TTL for KV cache. I’ll prepare a short runbook for the 3-day Dedicated test.

Link to test harness and sample scripts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-MedStream-Eval (read access granted).

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
